results.name: AWS Bets on Superblocks to Make Vibe Coding Safe for the Enterprise - Startup Fortune
results.content:
*AWS is giving Superblocks a cleaner route into enterprise cloud accounts, and the bet is that controlled AI app building will beat fast but loose vibe coding.*  
AWS Marketplace now lists Superblocks as a governed enterprise vibe coding platform deployed on AWS, while Superblocks published its Superblocks 3.0 release on July 28, 2026. The deal is simple. The risk is obvious. When an employee uses an outside app builder to turn a prompt into an internal tool, company data and access rules can move beyond the places IT already controls - and so can the model prompts behind them.  
Superblocks says its new private cloud setup can run inside a customer's AWS VPC, with app data and code kept in that private cloud. That matters. When a business user needs storage, the company says Superblocks can spin up Amazon Aurora or Amazon S3 infrastructure. For AI inference, the product runs through the customer's Amazon Bedrock account, using models the organisation has approved. That is the practical shift. If you run security, you don't have to choose between banning the tool and letting teams paste sensitive workflows into personal Replit or Lovable accounts.
## AWS already has coding tools, but this solves a different problem  
AWS isn't short of AI software products. Its Kiro documentation describes an agentic coding service that turns prompts into specs, code, docs and tests, built on Amazon Bedrock. Amazon Q Business is described in AWS documentation as a generative AI enterprise chat assistant, though AWS now says it stopped accepting new Q Business customers after July 31, 2026. Neither is aimed at the same person Superblocks is chasing. Superblocks wants the operations manager, finance analyst or support lead who knows the workflow but doesn't write production React code for a living.  
[LG Bets Its Actuators and Batteries on a Humanoid Robot Built With Nvidia](https://startupfortune.com/lg-bets-its-actuators-and-batteries-on-a-humanoid-robot-built-with-nvidia/)  
LG and Nvidia signed an MOU on August 13, 2026 to build LG's first bipedal humanoid robot, powered by Nvidia's Isaac GR00T model, Jetson Thor compute and Halos safety system, while LG supplies its own actuators, sensors and batteries. LG will test its wheeled CLOiD robot at a Tennessee washing machine plant this year ahead of a Q1 2027 humanoid...
## The real product is control  
Governance is the product. Superblocks says Clark uses specialist agents across design, IT, engineering, security and QA, applying company standards for permissions, SSO, audit logging, secrets management and package scanning as apps are built. The Superblocks 3.0 release also says the platform can restrict access to public NPM at the network level, connect to a private registry and maintain a software bill of materials for deployed apps. Speed was never enough. The app still has to survive security review.  
There is also a model-cost angle, though it shouldn't distract you from the bigger point. Superblocks says its Smart Router can break work into tasks and route them to different models, using frontier models for harder planning and cheaper open-weight models for routine coding. The company claims that can cut AI inference costs by up to 30%. Treat that as a vendor claim until customers prove it in production, but the direction is right. No serious enterprise wants one model provider welded into every internal workflow forever.
